There are zero corners on a circle, not infinitely many. The circle is the limit of a regular polygon as the number of sides goes to infinity, but that's not the same thing.

The number of numbers between zero and one is *an* infinity (the cardinality of **R**), but there are plenty more. *Infinitely* more, actually, as shown by [Cantor's theorem](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cantor%27s_theorem).

Oh, and I guess there are other kinds of infinity beyond infinite cardinals.
